subject: Pilot extension tradeoffs & performance-credit proposal — Arbor Health
messages:
From: Olivia Barnes <olivia@arborhealth.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Pilot status & runway request

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the support last week — the team made progress on the integration but we’re still seeing higher-than-expected token consumption during our long-form summarization tests. That means we’re not in a position to evaluate end-to-end product metrics (cost per call / latency SLOs) this week.

Two asks:
- Can we extend the POC by 3 weeks so we can finish the integration and run the full customer dataset?
- If an extension isn’t available at no cost, would Redwood consider either a credit to offset the additional tokens or a temporary discounted rate for the extension window?

I can share updated usage projections (I ran a quick forecast) — attaching the spreadsheet in my next email. Procurement needs a clear paper trail if there’s a change request, so if you have a simple addendum template that would help us move faster.

Appreciate the help,
Olivia Barnes
Head of Integrations
Arbor Health

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@arborhealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jan 2027 11:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Pilot status & runway request

Hi Olivia — thanks for the update and for the projected numbers you mentioned over the call.

We want to make sure you can complete the evaluation and get reliable unit economics, so here are three options we can move forward with quickly:

1) Short-extension (2 weeks) — no charge, one-time courtesy extension to finish the integration and run the core dataset.
2) Full-extension (3 weeks) — 15% discount on per-token billable units for the extension period.
3) Credit swap — convert unused portion of the original slot allocation into a one-time credit that you can apply to the next 45 days.

Each option has tradeoffs: 1) fastest to sign off but might be tight for your end-to-end tests; 2) gives you more runway but we’d need a light written addendum; 3) best if you think you will continue with a follow-on committed evaluation or conversion.

I’ve attached a simple worksheet (usage_projection.xlsx) I’d like you to confirm — it lets us calculate how credits or discounts map to your expected token delta. If you’re able to send procurement’s preferred route (discount vs. credit vs. signed extension), we’ll prepare the addendum tailored to that choice.

If helpful, Marissa can run the concession through our scorecard to confirm what discount level we can approve without legal review.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachment: usage_projection.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jan 2027 14:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Pilot status & runway request (internal)

Looping in Priyom to align on margin impact and approval path.

Kim — quick thoughts after reviewing Olivia’s ask and the worksheet:
- We should prefer a 3-week extension to avoid back-and-forth with the customer mid-run; it materially reduces risk of them not having statistically significant results.
- Counter: offer 3 weeks + 10% discount, conditional on Arbor committing to a 6-week Dedicated evaluation (not a purchase commitment, but a prioritized start date within 60 days). The commitment triggers onboarding credits worth ~5% of the anticipated first-month invoice.
- If procurement pushes back, we can fall back to a 2-week free extension (option 1) to buy time.

Proc/legal will need a short addendum. Marissa recommended language: single-clause amendment specifying extension dates, discount percentage, and a non-binding statement of intent for the Dedicated evaluation. We can have Legal turn that into an addendum and circulate for signature within 24 hours.

Quote from Kimberly’s message to Olivia for context: 
> Each option has tradeoffs: 1) fastest to sign off but might be tight for your end-to-end tests; 2) gives you more runway but we’d need a light written addendum; 3) best if you think you will continue with a follow-on committed evaluation or conversion.

Priyom — can you confirm we have capacity to prioritize a Dedicated evaluation slot for Arbor within 60 days if they accept? If not, we should adjust the counter.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Manager, Enterprise Sales Operations

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@arborhealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Arbor Health Procurement <procurement@arborhealth.ai>
Date: Tue, 26 Jan 2027 08:40:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Pilot status & runway request

Hi Olivia — following internal alignment, here’s the proposal we can put on paper today:

- Extension: 3 calendar weeks (runway extended from Feb 1 — Feb 21).
- Concession: 10% discount on billable tokens generated during the extension window.
- Conditional item: Redwood will prioritize a Dedicated evaluation slot for Arbor to start within 60 days; this is non-binding on your side but helps us plan capacity and triggers onboarding credits applied to the first month if you elect to proceed.

I’ve attached the short addendum (Redwood_POC_Addendum_v3.pdf) and a DocuSign link for your procurement team to sign. If this aligns with procurement’s preference we’ll mark the deal as an amended POC, send the DocuSign, and turn on the 3-week window as soon as we have the signed addendum.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/ARS-Addendum-7890

Please let me know if procurement prefers a credit instead of a percent discount — we can translate the discount into a fixed credit amount using the attached usage_projection.xlsx. Would you be able to confirm by end of week so we can avoid schedule slippage?

Thanks and looking forward to getting you the test results you need,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0123

Attached: Redwood_POC_Addendum_v3.pdf
